title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: October 10, 2026 - Weekend Market Summary (Reporting on October 9, 2026)

sections.title: Market Pulse: US Stocks Close Record-Setting Week with Gains

items.headline: U.S. stocks finished higher on Friday, capping a record-setting week across major indices, driven by positive sentiment ahead of the Q3 earnings season.
items.summary: The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq Composite all recorded gains on October 9, 2026. Investors showed cautious optimism despite fluctuating oil prices and rising Treasury yields, as attention shifts to upcoming corporate earnings and consumer inflation data.

items.headline: Crown Castle surges on SpaceX news
items.summary: Crown Castle International Corp. ($CCI) led gainers, rising 15.6% after SpaceX announced a purchase of low-band spectrum, potentially making Starlink Mobile a major U.S. mobile carrier, benefiting cell tower owners.

items.headline: Moderna extends gains
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) continued its strong performance, adding 14.2% on Friday and posting a 64.7% gain over the past month.

items.headline: Humana rallies on Medicare Advantage ratings
items.summary: Humana ($HUM) rallied 11.6% following encouraging data regarding its quality ratings for Medicare Advantage plans.

items.headline: T-Mobile US drops on competition concerns
items.summary: T-Mobile US ($TMUS) fell 13.3% amid competition concerns stemming from yesterday's SpaceX spectrum deal.

items.headline: AT&T slides amidst telecom competition
items.summary: AT&T ($T) declined 9.8%, also impacted by increased competition in the telecommunications sector following SpaceX's spectrum acquisition.

items.headline: Delta Air Lines misses earnings, cuts guidance
items.summary: Delta Air Lines ($DAL) slipped after reporting a miss on earnings estimates for the first time in two years and slashing its 2026 profit outlook due to persistent high fuel prices.

items.headline: Real Estate and Healthcare Lead Strong Sector Performance; Energy and Communications Services Lagged
items.summary: On Friday, Real Estate led all sectors with a 1.86% gain, followed by Healthcare at 1.58%. Consumer Discretionary also performed well, up 1.02%. Energy slipped 0.25% after recent outperformance, while Communication Services fell 1.62%. For the week, utilities (up 3.92%) and consumer defensives (up 3.89%) were the best performers, whereas industrials (down 0.87%) and technology (down 0.13%) lagged.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Dips, Inflation Expectations Rise Ahead of Fed Decision
items.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment fell to a five-month low in October, with inflation expectations reaching their highest levels since May. Markets are currently pricing in an approximately 83% probability that the Federal Reserve will maintain its benchmark rate this month, despite some economists anticipating another rate hike by year-end. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.24%.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Kicks Off with Major Bank Reports Next Week
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season is gaining momentum, with major banks including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and Bank of America scheduled to report results on Tuesday. Expectations are high, with S&P 500 earnings projected to jump over 30% for the quarter. Early reports indicate 84% of the initial 19 S&P 500 companies have beaten EPS estimates.

items.headline: Geopolitical Tensions and AI Optimism Influence Market Direction
items.summary: Geopolitical tensions, particularly related to the war with Iran, continue to affect oil prices, with Brent crude settling higher at $104.72 a barrel. Meanwhile, optimism surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) is providing a counterbalance to some market pressures, strengthening the corporate earnings outlook for semiconductor and 'Mag7' companies.
